cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses with a message for the Israelites. They are to present His food offerings at the appointed time, as a pleasing aroma to Him. Friend, I run six ovens on timers. When God says "appointed time," I sit up STRAIGHT.
First on the list: two year-old male lambs with no blemish. One lamb is offered in the morning.

cards.question: The first lamb is offered in the morning. When is the second lamb offered?
The LORD wants this pair of lambs offered every day, not just on feast days.

cards.text: Each lamb comes with fine flour mixed with olive oil and a drink offering, every amount measured out. Friend, that's a RECIPE, and I am taking NOTES.

cards.question: This daily burnt offering isn't brand new. Where does the LORD say it was established?

cards.text: Then comes the Sabbath day. Two unblemished year-old lambs go up, with a grain offering and a drink offering.

cards.question: On the Sabbath, those two lambs take the place of the regular daily offering.

cards.text: At the beginning of every month, the list grows: two young bulls, one ram and seven lambs, each with its own grain offering. Two bulls, a ram AND seven lambs. Friend, that's not an offering, that's a PARADE.

cards.question: This monthly offering is tied to something in the sky. When is it made?
Each month, one male ___ is also presented to the LORD as a sin offering.

cards.text: Now the yearly calendar kicks in. The fourteenth day of the first month is the LORD's Passover.

cards.question: The day after Passover, a seven-day feast begins. What is eaten for all seven days?
On the first day of this feast, Israel holds a sacred assembly and does no regular work.

cards.text: Every day of the feast: two young bulls, one ram, seven lambs and a male goat as a sin offering to make atonement. All of it on top of the regular morning offering, seven days in a row, and NOBODY gets to hit snooze.

cards.question: The feast reaches its seventh and final day. What does Israel hold that day?

cards.text: Next is the day of firstfruits, during the Feast of Weeks. Sacred assembly, no regular work.

cards.question: It's called the day of firstfruits. What does Israel present to the LORD that day?

cards.text: Same lineup again, two bulls, a ram, seven lambs and a goat to make atonement, and every animal must be unblemished. I spent years in a junk drawer, friend, so trust me, I know EXACTLY where the dented ones end up.
Now the seventh month, and its first day gets a sacred assembly with no regular work. But this day comes with its own sound.

cards.question: What is the first day of the seventh month a day for Israel to do?

cards.text: The offering: one young bull this time, one ram, seven lambs and a male goat as a sin offering to make atonement.

cards.question: Since this day is also the start of a month, its offering replaces the monthly one.

cards.text: On the tenth day of this seventh month, another sacred assembly. And this time it's not just no regular work. It's no work at ALL.

cards.question: On the tenth day of the seventh month, the Israelites are to ___ themselves.

cards.text: Same offering as the first of the month: one bull, one ram, seven lambs. The goat for a sin offering comes in addition to the sin offering of atonement.
Then on the fifteenth day comes another sacred assembly, and a feast to the LORD begins.

cards.question: The feast after Passover ran seven days. How long does this feast in the seventh month last?

cards.text: Day one, and the numbers EXPLODE: thirteen young bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs and a goat for a sin offering. Thirteen BULLS, friend. I run six ovens on my busiest day and I still need a nap.
Day two, and I'm counting again. Twelve bulls.

cards.question: The feast's bulls went from thirteen to twelve. What happens to the bull count on each day after that?

answers.text: It drops by one each day

cards.question: During this feast, the rams and lambs drop each day too, just like the bulls.

cards.text: When the seven days are done, there's an eighth day: a solemn assembly, with no regular work.

cards.question: How many bulls are offered on the eighth day?

cards.text: Then the LORD sums it up: present these offerings at your appointed times. Every day, every Sabbath, every month, every feast. Friend, this calendar is FULL.

cards.question: These scheduled offerings aren't the only ones. What do they come in addition to?
Moses tells the Israelites all of this, just as the LORD commanded him.

findings.problem: The whole passage is rules for offerings and feasts, which the docs list as a long stretch: one summary story card and no choice cards. Following that rule would leave the passage with almost no cards and no way to meet the rule that choice cards equal or outnumber story cards. The walkthrough instead treats each feast day as a moment and asks about offering details throughout.
findings.question: When an entire passage is a long stretch (here, rules for offerings and feasts), how should Prep handle it? Should each appointed day (daily, Sabbath, new moon, Passover and Unleavened Bread, Firstfruits, Trumpets, the tenth day, the seven-day feast and the eighth day) count as a moment that can get choice cards, while the offering counts and amounts are only summed up? Or does the passage need a different approach?

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences. It is over the limit of 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: the list, "Two bulls, a ram AND seven lambs." and the PARADE line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: the day one list, "Thirteen BULLS, friend." and the six ovens line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: the summary, "Every day, every Sabbath, every month, every feast." and "Friend, this calendar is FULL."

findings.problem: The card says "Same offering as the first of the month." In this passage, "the beginning of every month" (Numbers 28:11) is the monthly offering of two bulls, not one. The card means the first day of the seventh month (Numbers 29:2), but as written the comparison reads as untrue.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The card cites Numbers 29:37-39 but tells only 29:39 (present these at your appointed times). Verses 29:37-38, the eighth day's grain and drink offerings and its goat, aren't told.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The answer, that the rams and lambs don't drop each day like the bulls, depends on day one's two rams and fourteen lambs in Numbers 29:13. The card cites only 29:17-32.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: Numbers 29:17-34 is a repeated report: each day of the feast brings the same offering with one fewer bull. Cards 12 and 13 put choice cards on that stretch instead of summing it up on a story card.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: This card asks about the ram and lamb counts in the repeated daily reports of Numbers 29:17-32, which are a long stretch.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to recall an offering count (how many bulls on the eighth day). That is detail from the offering rules, not a moment that moves the passage. It also can't be reasoned out from the earlier cards.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: Of the stop's 10 choice cards, 6 are multiple choice, 3 are true or false and 1 is fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Of the stop's 9 choice cards, 5 are multiple choice, 3 are true or false and 1 is fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates by a wide margin, and the mix closely mirrors stop 1.
